summary: Parkevtate Vosianc turns on Pinterest, a stock he owned and ranked among his top 10 buys, after a third quarter of 12% revenue growth to $1.174B and a record 661M monthly active users that still disappointed: operating cash flow fell 2% and free cash flow fell 6%, and the shares dropped 7% on the print. He compares it unfavourably with Meta's 26% revenue growth and Reddit's 50%+, notes the 4M added US and Canadian users, but argues the company spent more to get its results, with $292M of stock compensation up 25% and little new product to show, and no Class A buyback in the quarter. The verdict is a stance flip: from BUY to a partial SELL, selling one-third of his shares, the tranche bought near $34, before year-end for tax-loss harvesting, while keeping the other two-thirds bought near $19. His DCF fair value is revised lower again to $30 against a price near $19, and he sees no catalyst for 2026, though he still calls the value one of the best in the market and flags a takeover at the $10.5B market cap as the bull case for holders. Call: PINS SELL (partial), a flip from BUY.
title: I'm Losing Confidence in Pinterest

calls.thesis: FLIP: was BUY (top-10, high conviction), now PARTIAL SELL — he is losing confidence in management's ability to unlock value in 2026 and will sell one-third of his shares (the tranche bought ~$34) before year-end for tax-loss harvesting, keeping the other two-thirds (bought ~$19). He still calls the value one of the best in the market, so this is a trim, not a full exit.
calls.base_case: Q3 revenue +12% to $1.174B, record 661M monthly users, but operating cash flow -2% and FCF -6%; Q4 guide ~$1.45B revenue (+10%).
calls.bull_case: Prime takeover target at a $10.5B market cap with 600M+ users; a buyer (he names Apple, Adobe, PayPal, Amazon, Walmart) or a leadership change could unlock value.
calls.bear_case: No catalyst seen for 2026; management keeps disappointing quarterly, R&D/stock comp keep rising ($292M stock comp, +25%) with little new product to show, and no buyback of Class A shares in the quarter.
